newsitem.title: CANADA: Repap Enterprises says reviewing bids.
newsitem.headline: Repap Enterprises says reviewing bids.

text.p: Repap Enterprises Inc said on Wednesday it was reviewing bids for its operating units and expected to give shareholders more information on the offers in July.
"We have received one or two bids at the last moment," Repap Chief Executive George Petty told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
Repap had set June 23 as the deadline for receiving bids for all of the company or any of its operating units in Canada and the United States.
Petty declined to specify how many bids were received or whether they were for all of the Montreal-based coated paper maker or for one or more of its operating units.
Repap has pulp and papermaking facilities in New Brunswick, Wisconsin, Manitoba and British Columbia.
Petty said Repap was in discussions with debt holders regarding its bank debt and convertible debentures coming due in July and August.
About C$270 million of debt Repap owed to two Canadian banks and another lender is due July 28. Repap also has US$130 million of convertible debentures maturing on August 1.
At April 30, consolidated debt at Repap's corporate level was C$2.3 billion.

Looking to the company's operating outlook, President Stephen Larson said the global market for groundwood coated papers was improving, especially in North America, because of strong magazine and advertising industries.
"Our shipments are running up 37 percent year-to-year and our inventory is down 50 percent to 67,000 tons," Larson said.
